title: Agent skills are the future of computer work
description: Start thinking of agent skills as little pieces of agentic software, because that is what they are and they might be the future of computer work. LLMs are natural language computers, and skills are the natural language software that runs on them, the same way traditional software runs on traditional computers. Instead of writing your logic in if statements and while loops you write it in plain language for the model to interpret, and there is almost no limit to the logic you can pack into one skill file. You can even drop real scripts inside a skill for the agent to execute with its bash tools. Granular skills plug into bigger skills exactly like software modules. Once you see skills as agentic software the whole thing clicks.
transcript: You need to start thinking of agent skills as little pieces of agentic software that might actually become the future of your computer work. Just like LLMs are like little natural language computers that you can analogize to traditional computers, skills are little pieces of natural language software that run within those natural language computers just like traditional software runs on traditional computers. Instead of defining steps programmatically in if-then loops or while loops, in a skill you're actually defining those steps in natural language to be interpreted by a large language model. The nice thing about defining these things in natural language is there's almost no limit to the amount of different loops and logic that you can include in an agent skill file. What's great about an agent skill file or folder is you can also include pieces of traditional software like scripts that your agent can execute with its bash tools. Once you start thinking of agent skills as agentic software, you understand how skills can modularly plug into each other where you can have more granular skills that only focus on the execution of one small task that plug into more complex skills that maybe chain multiple granular skills together just like traditional software. If you want to learn more about how to write, use, and optimize agent skills just like they are pieces of agentic software, I have full video courses on exactly that in my school community. The link is in my bio and I'd love to get learning with you.
